location: No step fails. The minor points are the unused count "There are ⌊y⌋−⌊z⌋ ≤ ⌊y⌋ ≤ b_f^{-1/d}x^{1/d} possible values of k" before (7), and the unlabelled constant C in (14).
objection:
I checked the whole proof against all eight checklist items and found no gap that cannot be trivially filled.

(i) Identifying R_f. P5 gives D_f=ζP_f for Re s>1, and P_f is holomorphic on Re s>−1/2. So Res_{s=1}D_f=P_f(1)=Σλ(r)ρ(r)/r, which is the coefficient in P4. B_f and K_f are defined identically in P6 and in the statement.

(ii) Hypotheses of P2, P3, P4 and P6 at the choices Z=x^θ, R=x^{2/a}. These hold once x_0(f) makes Z≥2 and R≥2: θ<1 and 2/a<1, z≥1 exists because f is increasing with f(1)≤Z, and every m=hf(k) satisfies m≤x.

(iii) The summed P3 error is right: f'(k)N_k x^{4/5+δ}≤x^{9/5+δ}f'(k)/f(k)≪x^{9/5+δ}/k, and summing over k≤y≪x^{1/d} gives x^{9/5+δ}log(2x).

(iv) Identity (11) is correct: x²(F(x/Y)−F(x/Z)) = −x²R_f log(Y/Z)+cx(Y−Z)+Z²Θ(x/Z)−Y²Θ(x/Y). I also re-derived P6's integral identity: ∫_Z^{x/h}(x−ht)dt=(x−hZ)²/(2h).

(v) Exponent bookkeeping:
- 1+θ(2−1/d)=(8d−3)/a=2−1/a.
- Z^{-1/d}R^{1/2}=R^{-1/2}=x^{-1/a}.
- (2−1/a)−(1/2+3d/a)=(6d−5)/(2a)>0.
- x²(x/Y)^{-13/8}=x^{3/8}Y^{13/8}.
- Every term in (19) is ≤x^{2−η+ε}, since η≤1/5, η≤1/a≤1/d and δ=ε/2.

(vi) The case Y<Z is handled by P2's initial-modulus bound together with (4). Both are monotone in Y, so the bound holds for every Y<Z, not only typical values.

(vii) Constants depend only on f and ε, and x_0 depends only on f. No external literature is used, and the deps are used exactly as stated.
other_issues: Cosmetic: the count of k values just before (7) is never used; only the bound y≪x^{1/d} matters, and only inside log y.
Cosmetic: the constant C in (14) is not labelled. It is absolute, so this is harmless.
Cosmetic: the hypothesis ε<η_d/2 in the statement is never needed; the argument works for any ε>0.
